entry.title: Enter the device code
entry.description: Your desktop app or terminal shows a 6-character code. Enter it here.
entry.footnote: No code on screen? Go back to the device and start authorization again.

add.kindLabel: Which kind of device are you adding?
add.kindHint: Browsers are not managed devices — no need to add one

install.downloadBody: Download the installer for that platform from GitHub Releases (macOS .dmg / Windows .exe / Linux .deb).

login.agentredTitle: Install agentred on that machine and sign it in
login.agentredDesc: Install the binary, then sign in straight away; registering the background service comes next — once the daemon is running, agentred login is refused outright. The server address is already this console's own address, so you can copy the command as is.
login.commandLabel: Same terminal, once it is installed
login.agentredTip1: The command prints a line reading User code: XXXXXX — that is the six-character device code.
login.agentredTip2: It also tries to open a browser; servers usually have none, so bring that code back here instead.
login.agentredTip3: The command keeps waiting until you approve it in step 2; only then does it exit and write the credentials on that machine.
login.agentredTip4: The device code expires; run the command again if it does. The approval screen counts down the time left.
login.desktopTitle: Install the Agentre desktop app on that computer and sign in to the same account
login.desktopDesc: Install the desktop app from GitHub Releases, then go to Settings → Remote → Sign in, using this console as the server address.
login.desktopTip1: The desktop app shows a six-character device code and tries to open a browser to authorize it.
login.desktopTip2: If no browser opens, or you would rather approve it on this computer, bring that code to step 2.
login.desktopTip3: The device code expires; start over from the desktop app if it does. The approval screen counts down the time left.

service.agentredTitle: Register agentred as a background service
service.agentredDesc: Do this last, once the device is approved: the service starts on boot, so the machine stays connected after you close the terminal.
service.commandLabel: That machine's terminal, once the device is approved
service.tip1: This has to come last: agentred login writes state.json only when you approve it. A daemon started any earlier holds the old, logged-out state.json in memory, and its next write silently overwrites that — the device looks authorized but never connects.
service.tip2: Running it again is harmless: the command is idempotent, it updates the configuration and makes sure the service is up.
service.desktopTitle: Nothing else to register for the desktop app
service.desktopDesc: The desktop app has agentred built in: it is online while the app is open, so there is no separate background service to register.

code.handoff: Submitting opens the approval screen, where you check the code against the device and approve it. Come back here for the last step once it is approved.
